note: The output field every agent must declare, the register-request block it is written in, and the format of the shared surface register. scripts/build-agents.py renders these into agents/, commands/ and the agents page, and scripts/build-agents.py --check and scripts/check-skills.py fail if an agent lacks the field or the instruction. scripts/register.py parses the block.

output_field.heading: Assumptions and open questions
output_field.rule: It is required. An explicit None. is allowed when there are none; leaving the section out is not.

request_block.line_rule: One line per entry: the type in capitals, a colon, a space and a one-line statement, all inside square brackets. TYPE is any type in register.types, upper-cased, so adding a type to register.types is a data change only. Put None. alone between the delimiters when there are no entries.
request_block.verbatim_rule: The block is identical whoever writes the register. Whoever writes it out copies each statement exactly: no summarising, merging, rewording, reordering or dropping.

tag_meaning.assumption: something you decided without being able to confirm it, and carried on with
tag_meaning.question: something you could not settle yourself and want answered, ideally with your recommended answer in the statement
tag_meaning.blocker: something that stops you finishing, or finishing correctly, until it is resolved

request_block.cannot_write_instruction: Agents that cannot write to the register themselves must emit the register-request block in their transcript. Any coordinator invoking such an agent must take those register requests as-is and write them out verbatim.

register.format: JSON Lines: one JSON object per line, UTF-8, append-only. Never edit or delete a line; a change of state is a new line.

declare.purpose: An agent declares an assumption it made, a question it could not answer, or a blocker. The text is the statement from its register-request block, verbatim.

update.purpose: The coordinator or the human changes the state of an earlier entry, or rates it.

impact.meaning: what goes wrong if the assumption or the recommended answer is wrong: low is cosmetic or easy to undo, medium is rework in one phase, high is a wrong product, security or data risk, or rework across phases. Optional: a block line carries no rating, so an entry is unrated until the coordinator rates it with an update line

urgency.meaning: how soon the human's view is needed: low can wait for the end of the cycle, medium is needed before later phases rely on it, high blocks the work. Optional, like impact

meaning.surfaced: Put in front of the human.
meaning.answered: The human answered, or confirmed or rejected the assumption.
meaning.dismissed: Settled from the repo or the brief, with the reason in note.
meaning.duplicate: Same as the entry in ref.

statuses.rule: An entry is declared with status open. Its current status is the status of the latest update line whose ref is its id.

via.meaning: who wrote the line: the agent itself, or the coordinator mirroring the agent's register-request block verbatim

aidev-po.purpose: aidev-po (https://github.com/mitulamin/aidev-po) defines the product upstream and writes this same register. Its lines use the baseline above plus the values and fields below, so a register goes to ai-sdlc-loop in an aidev-po gate bundle and comes back again, and both checkers pass it. ai-sdlc-loop's agents do not write these values, and they are not register-request block types. A register that uses none of them is a plain baseline register.
aidev-po.phase_values: aidev-po writes its stage in phase, in lower case: idea, audience, actors, systems, scope, workshops, presentations or fsd.

types.decision: a choice the human made, or aidev-po's coordinator made on the human's behalf, while defining the product. It is binding downstream: follow it, and raise a question rather than override it
types.feedback: the human's feedback on an aidev-po output; the full record is in the product's .po/feedback.jsonl, named in record
types.attribution: aidev-po's tracer's finding for a feedback entry; the full record is in the product's .po/attributions.jsonl, named in record

statuses.superseded: A decision replaced by a later one, named in ref.

item_ids.meaning: stable IDs of the output items the entry is about, such as REQ-012 or AC-003

record.meaning: the id of the full feedback or attribution record
